title: Understanding Average Acceleration
text: To find the average acceleration, you need to know the change in velocity and the time over which this change occurs.

title: Formula for Average Acceleration
text: The formula for average acceleration is given by: $$a=(v_{f}-v_{i})/t$$, $$where$$ $$v_{f}$$ is the final velocity, $$v_{i}$$ is the initial velocity, and $$t$$ is the time taken.

title: Initial and Final Velocities
text: Since the motorcycle starts from rest, the initial velocity $$v_{i}$$ is $$0\, \tfrac{\text{m}}{\text{s}}$$. $$The$$ $$final$$ $$velocity$$ $$v_{f}$$ is given as $$26.8\, \tfrac{\text{m}}{\text{s}}$$.

title: Calculate the Change in Velocity
text: Calculate the change in velocity using the formula: $$v_{f}$$-$$v_{i}$$.

title: Calculate the Average Acceleration
text: Now, use the formula $$a=(v_{f}-v_{i})/t$$ to find the average acceleration. Substitute $$v_{f}=26.8\,\tfrac{\text{m}}{\text{s}}$$, $$v_{i}=0\,\tfrac{\text{m}}{\text{s}}$$, $$and$$ $$t=3.90\, \text{s}$$.
